title: Fälle in Echtzeit
summary: The meta-module: how to survive the case system while actually talking — default, repair, and keep going

blocks.title: Warum du einfrierst — und warum das okay ist
blocks.body: Here's the honest truth about German cases: mid-sentence, your brain is trying to solve **four cases × three genders × two article types** in real time. That's a lot to compute before the next word. So you freeze on *der/dem/den* — **everybody does**, including advanced learners. Today isn't a grammar drill. It's a **survival module**: how to keep talking while your case-brain catches up. **The one new idea: you don't need to be correct to be understood.**
blocks.callout: The freeze isn't a flaw in you. It's just too much maths for the half-second you have.

blocks.title: Der Trick: sag's, reparier leicht, mach weiter
blocks.body: The move that separates a talker from a freezer is **default-and-repair**. **(1) Default:** pick an ending and say it, even if you're unsure. **(2) Repair:** if it felt wrong, do a tiny out-loud fix and move on — *„Ich gebe das dem… den… dem Mann.“* **(3) Keep going:** never stop. A self-correction sounds **fluent and human**, not like a mistake. What breaks a conversation isn't a wrong *den* — it's the ten-second silence while you hunt for the right one.

blocks.title: Rettungssätze — tap to hear your lifelines

items.nl: Moment, wie sagt man das noch?
items.en: Hang on, how do you say it again?
items.speak: Moment, wie sagt man das noch?

items.en: Let me think for a sec.

items.nl: Egal, du weißt, was ich meine.
items.en: Never mind, you know what I mean.
items.speak: Egal, du weißt, was ich meine.

items.nl: Dem, den… ach, du verstehst mich.
items.en: Dem, den… ah, you get me.
items.speak: Dem, den, ach, du verstehst mich.

pairs.right: „Ich gebe das dem… den… egal, dem Mann.“
pairs.note: The right version has a 'wrong' word in it — and it wins, because the conversation never stopped.
Compute-first freezes you. Speak-first keeps you in the room. Fix on the fly.

blocks.prompt: Du bist mitten im Satz und weißt plötzlich nicht: *der* oder *dem*? Was ist der beste Zug?
options: Warten, bis dir die richtige Form einfällt
blocks.explain: Default-and-repair keeps the conversation alive. Switching to English or freezing hands the moment away. Natives read the **meaning**; a stray *der/dem* almost never blocks it.

blocks.scene: You just got off the phone with your landlord and you're rattled — you fumbled every case.

lines.speaker: You
lines.nl: Ich habe eben mit dem Vermieter geredet und alle Fälle verwechselt.
lines.en: I just talked to the landlord and mixed up all the cases.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.nl: Na und? Hat er dich verstanden?
lines.en: So what? Did he understand you?

lines.speaker: You
lines.nl: Schon, aber ich habe ständig „den“ statt „dem“ gesagt.
lines.en: Yeah, but I kept saying 'den' instead of 'dem'.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.nl: Ehrlich, das merkt kaum jemand. Wir hören den Sinn, nicht die Endung.
lines.en: Honestly, hardly anyone notices. We hear the meaning, not the ending.
lines.spotlight: The core reassurance: natives decode **meaning**, and a wrong ending rarely blocks it.

lines.speaker: You
lines.nl: Aber ich friere jedes Mal ein, wenn ich nachdenken muss.
lines.en: But I freeze up every time I have to think.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.nl: Dann denk nicht nach. Sag's, reparier kurz, mach weiter. „Dem… den… egal.“ Fertig.
lines.en: Then don't think. Say it, fix it briefly, keep going. 'Dem… den… whatever.' Done.
lines.spotlight: Lena models default-and-repair out loud — exactly the move.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.nl: Genau. Ein falscher Artikel ist kein Beinbruch. Stillschweigen schon.
lines.en: Exactly. A wrong article is no big deal. Silence is.
lines.spotlight: *kein Beinbruch* = 'no broken leg', i.e. no big deal — a very German way to say relax.

blocks.prompt: Schreib deine zwei persönlichen Rettungssätze auf — die, die du beim nächsten Freeze wirklich sagen willst. Dann ein Satz dazu: *Ein falscher Fall ist kein Beinbruch, weil…*
